summary: The firstborn of a cow, sheep or goat is a bechor only if it belongs fully to a Jew. Kohanim and Levi'im do have this mitzvah, because they were freed only from redeeming a firstborn son and a firstborn donkey.

chunks.en: Someone who buys the unborn calf of a non-Jew's cow,
chunks.st: With regard to one who purchases the fetus of a cow that belongs to a gentile;

chunks.he: וְהַמּוֹכֵר לוֹ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי,
chunks.en: or sells his cow's unborn calf to a non-Jew, even though he is not allowed to,
chunks.st: one who sells the fetus of his cow to a gentile, even though one is not permitted to sell a large animal to a gentile;

chunks.en: or becomes partners with a non-Jew,
chunks.st: one who enters into a partnership with a gentile with regard to a cow or its fetus;

chunks.en: or takes a cow from a non-Jew to care for it,
chunks.st: one who receives a cow from
chunks.stMore: a gentile to tend to it in exchange for partnership in its offspring;

chunks.en: or gives his cow to a non-Jew to care for it,
chunks.st: and one who gives his cow to a gentile in receivership,
chunks.stMore: so that the gentile owns a share of the cow’s offspring;

chunks.en: the calf is not a bechor,
chunks.st: in all of these cases, one is exempt from the obligation of redeeming the firstborn offspring,

chunks.en: because the pasuk says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "the firstborns in Yisrael," but not those of others.
chunks.st: “I sanctified to Me all the firstborn in Israel, both man and animal” (Numbers 3:13), indicating that the mitzva is incumbent upon the Jewish people, but not upon others.
chunks.stMore: If the firstborn belongs even partially to a gentile, the sanctity of firstborn does not apply to it.

chunks.en: Kohanim and Levi'im must keep this mitzvah.
chunks.st: The mishna continues: The priests and the Levites are obligated
chunks.stMore: in the mitzva, i.e., their animals have firstborn sanctity,

chunks.en: They were not freed from the bechor of a kosher animal,
chunks.st: as they were not exempted from the mitzva of the male firstborn of a kosher animal;

chunks.he: (וְלֹא נִפְטְרוּ) אֶלָּא מִפִּדְיוֹן הַבֵּן וּמִפֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר:
chunks.en: they were freed only from redeeming a firstborn son and a firstborn donkey.
chunks.st: rather, they were exempted only from redemption of the firstborn son and from the redemption of the firstborn donkey.

summary: An animal that had a lasting blemish before it was made holy can be redeemed. After that it is almost like a regular animal, except for a bechor and ma'aser.

chunks.he: כָּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁקָּדַם מוּם קָבוּעַ לְהֶקְדֵּשָׁן,
chunks.en: All holy animals that had a lasting blemish before they were made holy,
chunks.st: All sacrificial animals in which a permanent blemish preceded their consecration
chunks.stMore: do not assume inherent sanctity and only their value is consecrated,

chunks.en: once they are redeemed, their babies can be a bechor, and the Kohen gets his gifts from them,
chunks.st: and once they were redeemed, they are obligated in the mitzva of a firstborn, i.e., their offspring are subject to being counted a firstborn, and in the priestly gifts of the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw,

words.note: Parts of the animal given to the Kohen.

chunks.en: and they become regular animals, to be sheared and to do work.
chunks.st: and they can emerge from their sacred status and assume complete non-sacred status in order to be shorn and to be utilized for labor. And

chunks.en: Their babies and their milk are allowed after they are redeemed.
chunks.st: their offspring and their milk are permitted after their redemption.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts them outside the Beis HaMikdash is not punished,
chunks.st: And one who slaughters them outside the Temple courtyard is exempt from karet,

chunks.en: and they do not make a temurah,
chunks.st: and those animals do not render an animal that was a substitute for them consecrated.

words.note: An animal that someone tried to swap for a holy animal; it becomes holy too.

chunks.en: and if they died, they may be redeemed,
chunks.st: And if these animals died before they were redeemed, they may be redeemed
chunks.stMore: and fed to dogs, and they do not require burial,

chunks.en: except for a bechor and ma'aser.
chunks.st: except for the firstborn and the animal tithe.
chunks.stMore: With regard to these two types of offerings, even if they were blemished before they became consecrated they assume inherent sanctity, like other offerings that were consecrated and subsequently became blemished.

words.note: Every tenth animal, which is holy.

summary: An animal that was made holy first and only later got a lasting blemish stays much holier. Even after it is redeemed, it cannot be sheared or used for work.

chunks.en: All animals that were made holy before they got a blemish,
chunks.st: And all sacrificial animals whose consecration preceded their blemish,

chunks.en: or that had a passing blemish before they were made holy,
chunks.st: or who had a temporary blemish prior to their consecration

chunks.he: וּלְאַחַר מִכָּאן נוֹלָד לָהֶם מוּם קָבוּעַ (וְנִפְדּוּ),
chunks.en: and later they got a lasting blemish and were redeemed,
chunks.st: and afterward developed a permanent blemish and they were redeemed,

chunks.en: their babies are not a bechor, and the Kohen does not get his gifts from them,
chunks.st: they are exempt from, i.e., their offspring are not counted, a firstborn, and from the gifts of the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw,

chunks.en: and they do not become regular animals, to be sheared and to do work.
chunks.st: and they do not completely emerge from their sacred status and assume non-sacred status in order to be shorn and to be utilized for labor.

chunks.en: Their babies and their milk are forbidden after they are redeemed.
chunks.st: And their offspring, which were conceived prior to redemption, and their milk, are prohibited after their redemption.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts them outside the Beis HaMikdash is punished,
chunks.st: And one who slaughters them outside the Temple courtyard is liable to receive karet,

chunks.en: and they do make a temurah,
chunks.st: and those animals render an animal that was a substitute for them consecrated.

chunks.en: and if they died, they must be buried.
chunks.st: And if these animals died before they were redeemed, they may not be redeemed and fed to dogs; rather, they must be buried.

summary: A Jew who takes animals from a non-Jew in a "tzon barzel" deal still owes the non-Jew for them, so their babies are not a bechor. The mishnah teaches which later babies are a bechor.

chunks.en: Someone who takes "iron sheep" from a non-Jew:
chunks.st: With regard to one who receives animals as part of a guaranteed investment from a gentile,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the Jew receives the animals to raise them and commits to pay a fixed price at a later date even if they die or their value decreases, and the offspring born in the interim are divided between the gentile and the Jew,

words.note: A deal where he must pay their full value no matter what happens to them.

chunks.en: their babies are not a bechor,
chunks.st: their direct offspring are exempt
chunks.stMore: from the mitzva of the firstborn if they give birth to a male,

chunks.en: but the babies of their babies are.
chunks.st: but the offspring of their direct offspring are obligated
chunks.stMore: in the mitzva of the firstborn if they gave birth to a male.

chunks.en: If he set up the babies in place of their mothers,
chunks.st: If the Jew established their offspring in place of their mothers for collection in case the mothers die,

chunks.en: the babies of the babies are not a bechor,
chunks.st: the offspring of their direct offspring are exempt

chunks.en: but the babies of their babies' babies are.
chunks.st: and the offspring of the offspring of their direct offspring are obligated.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: even for ten generations,
chunks.st: Even until ten generations,

chunks.en: they are not a bechor, because they all promise payment to the non-Jew.
chunks.st: the offspring are exempt, as they all serve as a guarantee for the gentile,
chunks.stMore: because if he does not receive the fixed payment for the animal, he will collect his debt from any offspring born to it or its offspring.

summary: If a sheep gives birth to a baby that looks like a goat, or the other way around, it is not a bechor, unless it looks a bit like its mother.

chunks.en: A sheep that gave birth to a baby that looks like a goat,
chunks.st: A ewe that gave birth to a goat of sorts

chunks.en: or a goat that gave birth to a baby that looks like a sheep,
chunks.st: and a goat that gave birth to a ewe of sorts

chunks.en: it is not a bechor.
chunks.st: are exempt from the mitzva of the firstborn.

chunks.he: וְאִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין, חַיָּב:
chunks.en: But if it has some of its mother's signs, it is a bechor.
chunks.st: And if the offspring has some of the characteristics of its mother, it is obligated in the mitzva of firstborn.
